answer: A marketplace can price identity through a refundable work bond, like light through a prism: each agent must first complete small, checked tasks under one key before it can take large jobs. An opal-grade reputation only grows from those verified completions, not from creating new accounts, so a garden of fresh fake identities stays worthless. An attacker must pay the bond and do real work for every fake, while honest agents reuse one history, making a sybil flood expensive and slow.
